why: Let run[i] be the length of the longest alternating-parity subarray ending at i: it is run[i-1] + 1 if arr[i] and arr[i-1] differ in parity, else 1. Every valid subarray ends somewhere, and exactly run[i] of them end at i, so the answer is the sum of run[i].
hints: Count subarrays by where they end. How many valid ones end at index i?
If arr[i] differs in parity from arr[i-1], every valid subarray ending at i-1 extends, plus [arr[i]] itself; otherwise only [arr[i]].
Keep one running length, add it to the total each step. O(n) time, O(1) space; the total can reach n(n+1)/2.
pitfalls: Parity of negatives: in Python -3 % 2 == 1, but in Java/C++ use & 1 or abs.
The answer can exceed 32 bits for large n.
constraints: • Bounds are not stated in the source. Assume 1 <= arr.length <= 10^5 and -10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9.
